drivingQuestion: Was R' Yohanan's ruling that knife-severed flesh is nullified by the hide said about the mishna's first clause (a whole olive-bulk) or only about its latter clause (two half olive-bulks)?
outcomeNote: The version attaching R' Yohanan's ruling to the mishna's first clause is upheld once his case is restricted, with Rav Pappa, to flesh spread thin over the hide.

segments.he: גְּמָ׳ אָמַר עוּלָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא פְּלָטַתּוּ חַיָּה, אֲבָל פְּלָטַתּוּ סַכִּין – בָּטֵיל.
segments.en: «GEMARA:» The mishna teaches that in the case of a hide of an unslaughtered carcass upon which there is an olive-bulk of flesh, the flesh is not nullified by the hide, and therefore one who touches a strand of flesh emerging from the flesh is ritually impure. With regard to this section of the mishna, «Ulla said» that «Rabbi Yoḥanan said:» The Sages «taught» this halakha «only» in a case where «an animal severed» the piece of flesh, e.g., a dog bite. «But» if a person used «a knife» to «sever» the flesh, the flesh «is nullified» by the hide because the person nullified the flesh via his action.

segments.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן לְעוּלָּא: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אֲפִילּוּ כְּתַרְטָא? אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִין. וַאֲפִילּוּ כְּנַפְיָא? אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִין. אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָאֱלֹהִים! אִם אָמַר לִי רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִפּוּמֵּיהּ – לָא צָיֵיתְנָא לֵיהּ.
segments.en: «Rav Naḥman said to Ulla: Did Rabbi Yoḥanan say» this halakha «even» with regard to a large piece of flesh the size of «a tarta,» i.e., a quarter of a kav? Ulla «said to him: Yes.» Rav Naḥman was surprised and asked: «And» did he say it «even» with regard to a piece of flesh the size of «a sifter?» Ulla «said to him: Yes.» Rav Naḥman swore and «said to him: By God!» Even «if Rabbi Yoḥanan had said» this statement «to me» directly «from his mouth, I would not have listened to him.»

segments.he: כִּי סְלֵיק רַב אוֹשַׁעְיָא, אַשְׁכְּחֵיהּ לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי אַמֵּי, אַמְרַהּ לִשְׁמַעְתָּיה קַמֵּיהּ: הָכִי אֲמַר עוּלָּא, וְהָכִי אַהְדַּר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן. אֲמַר לֵיהּ: וּמִשּׁוּם דְּרַב נַחְמָן חַתְנֵיהּ דְּבֵי נְשִׂיאָה הוּא, מְזַלְזֵל בִּשְׁמַעְתֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן?!
segments.en: «When Rav Oshaya ascended» from Babylonia to Eretz Yisrael «he found Rabbi Ami,» and «he said this halakha before him: This is what Ulla said and this is what Rav Naḥman responded to him.» Rav Oshaya «said to» Rabbi Ami: «And» just «because Rav Naḥman is the son-in-law of the family of the Nasi, can he demean the halakhic statement of Rabbi Yoḥanan?»

segments.he: זִמְנִין אַשְׁכְּחֵיהּ דְּיָתֵיב וְקָאָמַר לַהּ אַסֵּיפָא: הָיוּ עָלָיו שְׁנֵי חֲצָאֵי זֵיתִים – מְטַמְּאִים בְּמַשָּׂא וְלֹא בְּמַגָּע, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל. רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: לֹא בְּמַגָּע וְלֹא בְּמַשָּׂא.
segments.en: Another «time» Rav Oshaya «found» Rabbi Ami «sitting and saying this» halakha «with regard to the latter clause» of the mishna: If «upon» the hide «there were two half olive-bulks,» the hide «imparts» the «impurity» of an unslaughtered carcass «by means of carrying but not by means of contact» with the flesh, because he touches them separately and moves them together; this is «the statement of Rabbi Yishmael. Rabbi Akiva says:» It imparts impurity «neither by means of contact nor by means of carrying.»

segments.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא פְּלָטַתּוּ חַיָּה, אֲבָל פְּלָטַתּוּ סַכִּין – בָּטֵיל.
segments.en: With regard to this section of the mishna, «Rabbi Yoḥanan said:» The Sages «taught» Rabbi Yishmael’s opinion that the hide imparts the impurity of an unslaughtered carcass by means of carrying «only» in a case where «an animal severed» the half olive-bulks of flesh from the animal. «But» if a person used «a knife» to «sever» the half olive-bulks of flesh, the flesh «is nullified.» If Rav Naḥman had heard that the statement of Rabbi Yoḥanan was stated with regard to a case of half olive-bulks of flesh, he would not have been surprised that this halakha also applies to pieces of flesh that amount together to the size of a tarta or a sifter.

segments.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ מָר אַסֵּיפָא מַתְנֵי לַהּ? אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִין. וְאֶלָּא עוּלָּא אַרֵישָׁא אַמְרַהּ נִיהֲלַיְכוּ? אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִין. אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָאֱלֹהִים, אִי אָמַר לִי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בִּן נוּן מִשְּׁמֵיהּ – לָא צָיֵיתְנָא לֵיהּ!
segments.en: Rav Oshaya «said to» Rabbi Ami: «Does the Master teach» this halakha «with regard to the latter clause» of the mishna but not with regard to the first section of the mishna that discusses the case of a complete olive-bulk of flesh? Rabbi Ami «said to him: Yes. But did Ulla say to you» this halakhic statement of Rabbi Yoḥanan in Babylonia «with regard to the first clause» of the mishna? Rav Oshaya «said to him: Yes.» Rabbi Ami «said to him:» If so, Rav Naḥman was justified in his surprise at the halakha of Rabbi Yoḥanan. «By God,» even «if Joshua, son of Nun, had said» this halakha «to me in his name,» i.e., from his own mouth, «I would not have listened to him.»

segments.he: כִּי אֲתָא רָבִין וְכׇל נָחוֹתֵי, אַמְרוּהָ אַרֵישָׁא. וְאֶלָּא קַשְׁיָא? כִּדְאָמַר רַב פָּפָּא:
segments.en: «When Ravin and all those descending» from Eretz Yisrael «came» to Babylonia, «they stated» this halakha of Rabbi Yoḥanan «with regard to the first clause» of the mishna. The Gemara objects: «But» the matter is «difficult.» If an olive-bulk of flesh is nullified by being severed with a knife, the same should be true for larger measurements, such as a tarta, which is unreasonable, as people would not usually disregard such a large amount. The Gemara resolves this difficulty «in accordance with that which Rav Pappa said» with regard to a different matter:

The reference is «to a thin» layer of flesh attached to the hide. «Here, too,» the Gemara concludes that Rabbi Yoḥanan’s statement is referring «to a thin» layer of flesh attached to the hide. When a person severs such a piece of flesh along with the hide, even if the total volume of the flesh is an olive-bulk, or even a much larger measure, it is insignificant and is nullified by the hide.

moves.cueHe: אמר עולא אמר רבי יוחנן: לא שנו אלא
moves.summary: Ulla reports R' Yohanan narrowing the mishna: only flesh an animal tore off is not nullified.
moves.about: R' Yohanan's limitation of the mishna's ruling about flesh left on a carcass hide

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה רב נחמן לעולא: אמר רבי יוחנן אפילו כתרטא
moves.summary: Rav Nahman presses Ulla on how large a piece the ruling covers.
moves.about: whether R' Yohanan's nullification was said even of a piece as large as a tarta

moves.summary: Ulla confirms it twice, for a tarta and for a sifter.
moves.about: confirming that R' Yohanan said it even of a tarta

moves.cueHe: האלהים! אם אמר לי רבי יוחנן מפומיה
moves.summary: Rav Nahman swears he would not accept the ruling even from R' Yohanan himself.
moves.about: whether it was said even of a piece the size of a sifter

moves.cueHe: כי סליק רב אושעיא, אשכחיה ליה לרבי אמי
moves.summary: Rav Oshaya, arriving in Eretz Yisrael, recites the whole exchange before Rabbi Ami.
moves.about: Rav Oshaya ascended to Eretz Yisrael and found Rabbi Ami

moves.cueHe: ומשום דרב נחמן חתניה דבי נשיאה הוא
moves.summary: He protests that Rav Nahman's rank does not license demeaning R' Yohanan's teaching.
moves.about: reciting before Rabbi Ami the exchange between Ulla and Rav Nahman

moves.cueHe: זמנין אשכחיה דיתיב וקאמר לה אסיפא
moves.summary: On another occasion Rabbi Ami is found reciting the ruling on the mishna's latter clause.
moves.about: reciting the mishna's latter clause about two half olive-bulks

moves.cueHe: אמר רבי יוחנן: לא שנו אלא
moves.summary: In his version R' Yohanan's limitation is attached to the two half olive-bulks of the latter clause.
moves.about: R' Yohanan's limitation, as R' Ami teaches it — on the mishna's latter clause

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה מר אסיפא מתני לה
moves.summary: Rav Oshaya asks whether Rabbi Ami teaches it only on the latter clause.
moves.about: whether Rabbi Ami teaches the ruling only on the mishna's latter clause
confirming that he teaches it only on the latter clause

moves.summary: Rav Oshaya confirms that Ulla said it on the first clause.
moves.about: confirming that Ulla reported it on the first clause

moves.summary: Rabbi Ami asks in turn whether Ulla gave it to the Babylonians on the first clause.
moves.about: whether Ulla told the Babylonians the ruling on the mishna's first clause

moves.cueHe: האלהים, אי אמר לי יהושע בן נון משמיה
moves.summary: Rabbi Ami himself refuses the first-clause version, vindicating Rav Nahman.
moves.about: R' Ami would not accept the nullification ruling as said of the mishna's first clause even from Joshua son of Nun

moves.cueHe: כי אתא רבין וכל נחותי, אמרוה ארישא
moves.summary: All who descended from Eretz Yisrael nevertheless reported it on the first clause.
moves.about: Rav Pappa's distinction of flesh spread thin over the hide, said with regard to another matter

moves.summary: But then the difficulty about a very large piece stands.
moves.about: if even an olive-bulk severed by a knife is nullified by the hide, so too a tarta, which is implausible

moves.summary: As Rav Pappa said elsewhere — the case is flesh spread thin over the hide, and so here too.
moves.about: R' Yohanan's ruling speaks only of flesh spread thin over the hide, so even a large bulk is insignificant
